rules: Use CacheManager for independent process-local caches; consider SharedCacheManager for repeated reads across trusted same-host workers. Measure latency, CPU and total memory on your workload; sharing adds owner and miss costs.
Import synchronous managers from client_query_cache for pymongo.MongoClient; import asyncio managers from client_query_cache.asynchronous for pymongo.AsyncMongoClient.
Create cached views with manager.get_cached_collection(collection) or manager[database][collection]. Supply collections from the manager's own client; retain views for repeated use.
Use cached views for find_one, find, aggregate, count_documents, estimated_document_count and distinct. Use the original PyMongo collection or .raw for writes, administration and other methods.
Treat find() and aggregate() results as native cursor subclasses, not lists. With asyncio, await single-result reads and aggregate(), but not find(); use async iteration or await cursor.to_list().

Fully consume cursors successfully to permit cache admission; close abandoned cursors. Started hit cursors retain their snapshot through invalidation, eviction and manager closure; start a new execution for a new lookup.

Do not assume a cached read observes a completed write: change-stream invalidation is asynchronous, with no catch-up barrier or guaranteed delay. Eligible misses use primary, majority reads; this does not make hits current.

Use direct PyMongo reads with suitable sessions and concerns for read-after-write, current authorization or required server execution. Hits skip execution and fresh server errors; direct reads do not refresh cached entries.

Expect ineligible requests, including sessions, incompatible options, unsafe queries and unavailable streams, to run through PyMongo and still fail if MongoDB is unavailable. Oversized results return uncached. A successful response does not prove caching.

Reuse a long-lived client and manager within each worker, never per request. Each CacheManager has independent data and streams. Close managers before their caller-owned clients; await asyncio close() or use async with.
Start one SharedCacheServer in the parent and pass only its connection to workers; each worker creates its own client and SharedCacheManager. Do not start a server in each worker lifespan.
Stop shared workers before closing their parent-owned server. Never reuse clients, managers or server handles inherited after fork; create worker clients and managers after process startup.
Construct and use asyncio SharedCacheManager in one running event loop. Enter it with async with or await SharedCacheManager.attach(client, connection) before reading; do not await its constructor.

Check shared-read eligibility: shared caching requires portable keys, standard dict documents, no custom codec registry and simple explicit/default collation; aggregates must stay within one collection. Other requests fall back to PyMongo.

Preserve all query and authorization predicates when using either manager. Never remove tenant filters or change query semantics to obtain cache hits; credential or role changes alone do not invalidate cached documents.

Keep SharedCacheConnection private: never log or persist it. Share only among trusted workers using the same MongoDB deployment, credentials and read visibility; holders can read all configured databases and submit cached values.

Use Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.28+; shared hosts also need Linux 5.1+, memfd sealing and /proc. For caching, use MongoDB 8.0+ replica sets or sharded clusters with collection reads, metadata and database-level changeStream access.

Size memory from measured peaks across workers and the shared owner; BSON budgets do not cap RSS or container memory. Distinguish capacity eviction from freshness: change streams invalidate data, while LRU eviction frees capacity.
